our-experience-e17.p_3: Attract new adult students to English-language programmes run by a Japanese education company. The hardest part was conveying why English mattered for Japan’s place in a more globalized world.

our-experience-e17.p_5: Several new adult students enrolled through his work, and three colleagues were trained under him. No enrolment figures are reported.
our-experience-e17.p_7: Presenting an offer convincingly to Japanese customers and colleagues, and helping others meet the standards a Japanese organization expects.

our-experience-e18.p_2: Connecting market needs with a practical direction for product development.
our-experience-e18.p_3: Help a technology business assess the market opportunity for its construction project collaboration platform, understand its existing capabilities and determine how the platform should evolve.
our-experience-e18.p_4: Shyam and Mak worked with the business on a market assessment, a diagnostic of the platform’s current capabilities and an evolution strategy.
our-experience-e18.p_5: The work brought the market and product perspectives together: what the platform could address, what it could already support and where further development was needed.
our-experience-e18.p_6: A platform evolution strategy supported by a two-year phased roadmap, providing a sequence for development rather than treating every improvement as an immediate priority.
our-experience-e18.p_7: The company’s platform evolution is underway through the phased roadmap. Implementation remains in progress; the case describes assessment and strategic direction, not completed commercial results.
our-experience-e18.p_9: Combining market assessment and capability diagnostics into an actionable development roadmap.

our-experience-e19.p_2: Using business relationships to develop market-entry opportunities—and recognising when conditions require a pause.
our-experience-e19.p_3: Help a consulting and technology business develop an entry into Turkey through a prospective client engagement and a local business partnership.
our-experience-e19.p_4: Drawing on Shyam’s network, the team connected with two chief executives and developed two potential routes into the market.
our-experience-e19.p_5: One involved a consulting and transformation engagement with an industrial minerals producer. The other involved a joint-venture strategy with a data services company.
our-experience-e19.p_6: Shyam and Mak worked with the business to develop these opportunities beyond initial introductions, connecting prospective relationships with engagement and partnership strategies.
our-experience-e19.p_7: Two developed market-entry opportunities: a proposed consulting and transformation engagement, and a joint-venture strategy.
our-experience-e19.p_8: Both advanced towards potential agreement but did not close. According to the contributors, shipping-cost pressures and currency and inflation uncertainty affected the conditions for proceeding. Both opportunities remain on hold.
our-experience-e19.p_10: Relationships must develop into workable business propositions, and timing must remain commercially sensible as conditions change.

our-experience-e20.p_3: Help a consulting and technology business define an international expansion strategy across ten markets in Asia, Europe and the Middle East.
our-experience-e20.p_4: Shyam and Mak worked with the business to refine how its consulting, transformation, innovation and technology services could combine with its solutions portfolio.
our-experience-e20.p_5: The strategy considered the mix of services and solutions across the ten markets, connecting what the business could offer with where it intended to grow.
our-experience-e20.p_6: A market expansion strategy linking the service and solution portfolio with a ten-market growth agenda and a seven-year valuation ambition.
our-experience-e20.p_7: The strategy was developed. The financial ambition was a planning target, not an achieved valuation or guaranteed result. Realisation depends on execution and market conditions.
our-experience-e20.p_9: Bringing market choices and the business offer together within a common growth strategy.

our-experience-e21.p_2: Connecting a regional proposition with media visibility, business outreach and first-hand engagement.
our-experience-e21.p_3: Help an Indian state position two of its cities as destinations for offshore development centres, highlighting their infrastructure, talent pool and government incentives.
our-experience-e21.p_4: As CEO and Chief of Strategy at a public relations and business consulting firm, Shyam developed an integrated communications and business-engagement strategy.
our-experience-e21.p_5: Working with the state’s IT department and appointed strategy partners, he shaped messages and supporting material for Indian and international media, planned roadshows to engage prospective businesses directly, and organised visits for company representatives to assess the destination first-hand.
our-experience-e21.li_2: Roadshows across five Indian cities and two US cities.
our-experience-e21.li_4: Site visits for representatives of more than 100 IT-services companies, to experience the destination first-hand.
our-experience-e21.p_7: Translating regional strengths into a proposition businesses can assess, supported by targeted communication and direct engagement.

our-experience-e22.p_2: Supporting market growth through sustained visibility, industry engagement and customer experience.
our-experience-e22.p_3: Help an Indian manufacturer of twin-screw extrusion machinery strengthen its international reputation and support expansion, particularly in the United States and Japan.
our-experience-e22.p_4: The business had an established presence in India and offices in both overseas markets. Its next stage of growth called for stronger recognition among prospective customers and a network of agents to support marketing and sales.
our-experience-e22.p_5: As a partner at a business consulting firm, Shyam was a key member of the team working with company leadership on its reputation and market-growth strategy.
our-experience-e22.p_6: The work combined consistent brand exposure, speaking engagements, trade-show participation and customer engagement. Personalised visits to the company’s experience centre gave prospective customers an opportunity to understand its manufacturing capabilities and assess its machinery first-hand.
our-experience-e22.p_7: The positioning drew on the company’s integrated manufacturing foundation and emphasis on quality and delivery.
our-experience-e22.p_8: Between 2014 and 2020, the company strengthened its international visibility and its engagement with prospective customers. According to Shyam, the company’s total revenue doubled over the period.
our-experience-e22.p_9: Shyam contributed to the wider effort by helping company leadership develop its market reputation and sustain engagement with prospective customers. The revenue growth reflected the company’s overall performance, not the consulting work alone.
our-experience-e22.p_11: Connecting technical strengths with sustained market exposure and direct customer experience.

our-experience-e23.p_2: Language, cultural understanding and trust that brought customers back, with their friends.
our-experience-e23.p_3: Increase sales at a menswear retailer’s main store in downtown Chicago between 2011 and 2013, including by attracting the many international visitors drawn to the city by tourism and global events.
our-experience-e23.p_4: Raju’s familiarity with different cultures and languages helped him serve the store’s international customers.
our-experience-e23.p_5: His ability to speak Japanese and understand the Japanese way of doing business built trust with Japanese visitors. One Japanese client returned the following year with friends, and this happened several times, gradually building a clientele of Japanese visitors whose purchases were larger than the store’s usual average.
our-experience-e23.p_6: Several customers came to the store asking for Raju, and chose to wait for him when he was busy.
our-experience-e23.p_7: He was told that his sales contributed to an increase of approximately 19% in the store’s overall sales. The period and basis of that figure were not specified.
our-experience-e23.p_9: Earning the trust of Japanese customers through language and cultural understanding, and turning that trust into referrals and repeat business.

our-experience-e24.p_2: Two systems that freed time for more productive work.
our-experience-e24.p_3: At a vacation-rental hospitality business, Raju’s team was struggling to keep up with following up with potential guests, and arrival instructions had to reach every guest.
our-experience-e24.p_4: Raju personally designed and implemented two systems:
our-experience-e24.li_1: An automated follow-up system for potential guests.
our-experience-e24.li_2: An automated arrival-instruction workflow. An automated agent checks twice a day for guests whose identity confirmation has come in and been verified, and sends those guests their arrival instructions.
our-experience-e24.li_3: Guest follow-up: by Raju’s estimate, at least 12 hours a week freed for more productive work.
our-experience-e24.li_4: Arrival instructions: by Raju’s estimate, three to six hours a week saved.
our-experience-e24.p_5: These are separate estimates for the two systems.
our-experience-e24.p_7: Spotting repetitive customer-service work and designing practical automation that frees people for higher-value tasks.

our-experience-e25.p_2: Pricing an incentive around a clear commitment, and building a lasting customer relationship.
our-experience-e25.p_3: A guest asked a vacation-rental business for a discount, explaining that he could bring together other parents who travelled each summer to the same region for their children’s sports tournaments. The business operated on low margins.
our-experience-e25.p_4: Raju, who had responsibility for such decisions, offered the guest preferential pricing on condition that he provided a commitment of at least 50 rooms. In later years he continued to offer a preferential arrangement on the same condition.
our-experience-e25.p_5: The arrangement began in 2017 and continued in later years. 2026 is expected to be its final year. According to Raju, it brought summer business that the company would otherwise not have had, and a lasting relationship with the guest.
our-experience-e25.p_7: Structuring a commercial incentive around a clear commitment, and building customer relationships that bring repeat business.

our-experience-e26.p_2: Visibility and set-up support for a series of chip-design businesses scaling up in India.
our-experience-e26.p_3: From the mid-2000s, a series of venture-funded fabless semiconductor start-ups, designing chips for wireless and broadcast communications, set up in India. Each needed to attract experienced engineers quickly, which called for high visibility.
our-experience-e26.p_4: As chief executive of a public relations firm, Shyam worked with the leadership of three such companies, in a series of separate assignments.
our-experience-e26.p_5: He shaped their messages and positioning, and arranged media interviews with their prominent investors explaining what each company was doing and how its work could transform communications and networking systems.
our-experience-e26.p_6: From the companies’ first days, he also helped coordinate their set-up in India and the support they needed to operate.
our-experience-e26.p_7: According to Shyam, each company grew to about 100 employees within six months. That growth reflected each company’s wider efforts; Shyam’s work supported its visibility, recruitment and set-up.
our-experience-e26.p_9: Building visibility that helps new technology businesses attract talent, and coordinating the practical steps of setting up in India.

our-experience-e27.p_2: A neutral platform where destinations presented their ecosystems and companies set out their requirements.
our-experience-e27.p_3: As global brands and technology-services companies expanded their presence in India, Indian states sought to attract them, and companies needed meaningful conversations to decide where to establish operations.
our-experience-e27.p_4: Through his social enterprise, Shyam created a business-destination platform where state governments could showcase their ecosystems and companies could hold meaningful conversations about setting up operations.
our-experience-e27.p_5: He personally designed the engagement formats, in which government officials listened to the requirements of corporate location decision-makers and helped them set up operations. He did not lobby companies to favour one state over another; the decision was left entirely to the companies.
our-experience-e27.p_6: Over three years, business-destination summits were held in 11 cities, each highlighting the strengths of its city. Shyam then decided to withdraw, as representing governments could conflict with the platform’s neutrality.
our-experience-e27.p_8: Designing neutral forums in which governments and companies can set out what each needs.

our-experience-e29.p_7: Finding the right counterparty and negotiating terms that reflect what owners and employees need from a transition.

our-focus.p_2: We are initially focusing on three opportunity areas: global capability centres, water solutions, and recycling and waste management.
our-focus.p_3: In each, we see possibilities for Japanese and Indian businesses to combine their strengths. Our role is to help identify a worthwhile opportunity, bring suitable participants together and develop a practical way forward.
our-focus.p_4: These are starting priorities. Our focus will evolve as we build relationships, deepen our understanding and explore new opportunities.
our-focus.p_5: Connecting Japanese business needs with capabilities in India—from exploring the possibilities to developing the partnerships and operating arrangements needed to deliver.
our-focus.p_6: Bringing together technology, local knowledge and delivery capabilities to address water needs and develop workable business opportunities.
our-focus.p_7: Connecting businesses and partners to recover resources, improve waste management and develop commercially viable solutions.
our-focus.p_8: We welcome conversations about other areas where Japanese and Indian strengths could create value together.

our-focus-global-capability-centres.span_2: In this section: Global capability centres
our-focus-global-capability-centres.p_3: For a Japanese business, establishing a global capability centre in India is more than a location decision. It starts with deciding what the centre should contribute—and what capabilities, relationships and operating arrangements would make that possible.
our-focus-global-capability-centres.p_4: The opportunity could involve technology, engineering, research, business operations or other specialist functions. The right approach depends on the business’s objectives, its readiness to work across borders and the responsibilities it wants to retain or share.
our-focus-global-capability-centres.li_1: What should the centre help the business achieve?
our-focus-global-capability-centres.li_2: Which capabilities should it develop, and how should they connect with teams in Japan?
our-focus-global-capability-centres.li_3: Should the business establish its own operation, work with a partner or develop the capability in stages?

our-people-mak.p_4: Connecting business growth, global markets and practical execution.
our-people-mak.p_5: Mak brings more than thirty years of experience in entrepreneurship, management consulting and business transformation. His work connects three questions: where a business can grow, what needs to change, and how to turn the opportunity into action.
our-people-mak.p_6: Mak began his entrepreneurial career helping manufacturers enter overseas markets, developing market strategies, customer relationships, distribution channels and cross-border sourcing arrangements.
our-people-mak.p_7: He subsequently held consulting leadership roles at PwC, Infosys Consulting and Accenture. His work has spanned market development, customer experience, sales and service innovation, operating models and technology-enabled transformation, from focused advisory assignments to complex global programmes.
our-people-mak.p_8: He has developed business cases, shaped commercial arrangements and led multidisciplinary teams through implementation, keeping the commercial opportunity connected to the people, capabilities and decisions needed to make it work.
our-people-mak.p_9: Born and raised in India, Mak studied and built much of his career in the United States. He also lived and worked in Japan for a year, developing an enduring affection for its people and culture.
our-people-mak.p_10: Work, education and travel across more than eighty countries have shaped his curiosity about how people build relationships and conduct business. He maintains strong personal ties to India and brings a global perspective to his commitment to the Japan–India relationship.
our-people-mak.p_11: At SetuHashi, Mak brings together business strategy, opportunity development and the coordination of complex undertakings. Working alongside Raju and Shyam, he is committed to helping Japanese and Indian businesses combine their strengths, develop worthwhile opportunities and carry them forward.

our-people-raju.p_4: Connecting people, markets and business expectations.
our-people-raju.p_5: Raju connects what customers expect with what businesses deliver. His work in sales and customer service, in Japan and the United States, centres on understanding people, earning trust and developing lasting business relationships.
our-people-raju.p_6: Raju began his working life in Japan. In a bespoke tailoring business he checked finished suits before delivery against what customers had been promised; in a Japanese education company he explained programmes to prospective adult students in Japanese, signed up new students and later trained newer colleagues.
our-people-raju.p_7: In the United States, he developed business customers across several regions for a maker of custom carpets produced in India. He translated what buyers specified into precise production instructions for weavers in India, standardized how clients chose colours, and coordinated imports and delivery.
our-people-raju.p_8: His later work in retail and hospitality has centred on serving people across cultures and languages, including leading a guest-services team. Drawing on that lived experience, he also helps individuals and teams prepare to work with Japan: its business etiquette, communication and workplace expectations.
our-people-raju.p_9: Born and raised in Japan, Raju maintains a deep affection for its language, people and everyday life. His Indian heritage and years in the United States add perspectives that help him relate to people across different backgrounds.
our-people-raju.p_10: These connections underpin Raju’s commitment to bringing Japanese and Indian businesses closer together. He brings understanding of Japanese customers and working practices, practical commercial experience and a relationship-centred approach. Working alongside Shyam and Mak, he helps businesses understand one another and build the confidence needed to explore opportunities together.

our-people-shyam.p_4: Connecting businesses, relationships and opportunities for growth.
our-people-shyam.p_5: Shyam brings more than thirty years of experience in entrepreneurship, business growth, strategic communications and international partnerships, with an extensive network across businesses, industry associations and public institutions.
our-people-shyam.p_6: Shyam has advised business owners and leadership teams on market development, positioning and expansion. His work includes helping international businesses enter India and supporting Indian businesses pursuing opportunities in the United States and Europe.
our-people-shyam.p_7: His experience spans technology, advanced engineering, infrastructure, health and wellness. Alongside advisory work, he has founded and operated ventures, developed international relationships, and negotiated licensing and manufacturing arrangements with European partners.
our-people-shyam.p_8: He has also worked at the intersection of business and public institutions, helping organizations navigate stakeholder relationships, regulatory questions and the practical conditions for growth.
our-people-shyam.p_9: Born and raised in India, Shyam brings a close understanding of its entrepreneurial environment, particularly Bengaluru’s business ecosystem, where he is based. He enjoys connecting people and organizations whose capabilities, ambitions and relationships can create possibilities together.
our-people-shyam.p_10: At SetuHashi, Shyam brings entrepreneurial energy, business relationships and practical knowledge of India. Working alongside Raju and Mak, he is committed to helping Japanese and Indian businesses recognize complementary strengths, build productive relationships and turn opportunities into business.

who-we-are.span_2: In this section: Our founding story
who-we-are.p_2: Raju, Shyam and Mak arrived at SetuHashi through different experiences—in Japan, India and around the world—but shared a commitment to contribute to two countries that matter deeply to them: India and Japan.
who-we-are.p_3: Changing international relationships and a desire for a new entrepreneurial chapter prompted them to consider what they could build together.
who-we-are.p_4: Longstanding personal connections brought them into conversation. When the three met in Bengaluru, that shared ambition became the basis for SetuHashi.
who-we-are.p_5: Research and early business conversations gave that ambition a practical direction: helping Japanese and Indian businesses turn complementary strengths into opportunities.
who-we-are.p_6: Raju brought his Japanese upbringing, Indian roots and extensive US experience in sales and customer service.
who-we-are.p_7: Shyam brought entrepreneurship and relationships across India’s business ecosystems.
who-we-are.p_8: Mak brought cross-border entrepreneurship and global experience in business growth and transformation.
who-we-are.p_9: We wanted to build a bridge between India and Japan—connecting businesses and people, developing opportunities and helping turn them into business. Our shared commitment became SetuHashi.
who-we-are.metaTitle: Our founding story — Who we are — SetuHashi

who-we-are-mission.p_1: We see extraordinary possibilities where Japan and India meet—and we refuse to let them remain merely possibilities.
who-we-are-mission.p_2: We are building SetuHashi to bring together the ambition, ingenuity and strengths of both worlds; to inspire trust, open new horizons and turn shared aspirations into achievements that matter.
who-we-are-mission.p_3: We want to be more than a bridge between Japan and India.
who-we-are-mission.p_4: We want to help build what comes next.
who-we-are-mission.metaTitle: Our mission — Who we are — SetuHashi

who-we-are-why-setuhashi.h1_1: Understanding both sides. Connecting opportunity to action.
who-we-are-why-setuhashi.p_2: Japanese and Indian businesses can bring together capabilities, ambitions and market access to reach new customers, strengthen operations and create new business—in either country and beyond.
who-we-are-why-setuhashi.p_3: A promising connection is only the beginning. Businesses also need to understand one another, establish a workable commercial basis and organize what happens next.
who-we-are-why-setuhashi.p_4: SetuHashi brings together personal connections to India and Japan, experience developing businesses across markets, and the ability to help put plans into action. We work across both sides of an opportunity and bring in relevant capabilities as the work requires.
who-we-are-why-setuhashi.p_5: Our commitment is to help build business relationships that work in practice and create value for those involved.
who-we-are-why-setuhashi.label_4: Connection → Mutual understanding → Workable commercial basis → Next steps organized → Plans in action

who-we-serve-government.p_3: Connecting public priorities with business possibilities.
who-we-serve-government.p_4: Governments and public agencies can help create the conditions for business collaboration. SetuHashi can help connect priorities in Japan and India with relevant businesses, capabilities and opportunities, and support the work needed to develop them.
who-we-serve-government.p_5: This includes national, state, prefectural and local bodies and public agencies, particularly economic-development and investment-promotion teams. Our involvement can focus on a region, an industry sector or a specific business initiative.
who-we-serve-government.h2_1: How we may work with government
who-we-serve-government.p_6: Commissioning a defined piece of work, such as an opportunity assessment for a region or sector.
who-we-serve-government.p_7: Taking part in, or helping to enable, an initiative that businesses are developing.
who-we-serve-government.p_8: Supporting regional and sector collaboration between Japanese and Indian businesses.
who-we-serve-government.h2_6: Develop opportunities for your region or sector
who-we-serve-government.p_9: Clarify regional strengths and priorities, and identify the sectors and business counterparts where collaboration could work.
who-we-serve-government.h2_7: Connect with businesses and investment prospects
who-we-serve-government.p_10: Identify relevant businesses and prospective investors, prepare the engagement and support the discussions that follow.
who-we-serve-government.p_11: Help an initiative work out which public bodies may be relevant, what they may need to see, and how to prepare.
who-we-serve-government.p_12: The aim is better-targeted engagement, the right counterparts, clearer requirements and initiatives that are more workable in practice.
who-we-serve-government.p_13: Public-sector engagement may matter, for example, for global capability centres (GCCs), water solutions or recycling. Requirements differ from one initiative to the next; not every initiative needs the same approvals, funding or support.
who-we-serve-government.p_14: These are ways we could work with public bodies. They do not describe existing government assignments or imply privileged access, and we cannot guarantee approvals, funding, incentives or investment. Governments and businesses make their own decisions; qualified specialists handle applicable legal, regulatory and financial matters.
